main_body: Flat paving/cobble ground patch (terrain tile, 64x48) in stone-brick pattern, seen top-down as a floor surface
top_band: none; the scan shows repeating paving-block rows (light 1-row highlight, mid grey-brown body, dark mortar line), not a raised object top
evidence: Terrain ground paving is a flat floor surface, not a standing object. The 3/4 contract for standing objects does not apply. The column scan shows a repeating brick/paving pattern with mortar lines, which is correct for a floor tile. No standing volume, so no top/front split is required.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 4 distinct colours and a median of 4 per tile, against 26 for the grass and 80 distinct colours. Its 5x5 flat-fill coverage is 44%, while both references have 0%. All dark edge pixels (100%) are neutral, so the mortar lines read as a neutral grey-black rather than a tinted material tone. The paving reference is also a low-colour piece (7 colours), but it has per-stone highlights and stones shaded one by one. The candidate repeats identical blocks with large flat areas of one tone, with only a few highlight dots, so it looks thinner and flatter than the references.
